sheet-113.description: Sheet 113 covers the centre of Millburn village (printed Milburn) on both sides of Main Street, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The Morris and Essex Division of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad crosses the top of the sheet on an embankment, with platforms and the Milburn passenger depot north of the tracks and C. H. Roll's coal and lumber yard with a coal pocket trestle just south of them. Main Street runs down the middle of the sheet from the railroad past Elm Street, which leaves it to the west, to Milburn Avenue (Springfield Avenue), which crosses the sheet near the bottom, and on to Taylor Street at the bottom edge. The west side of Main Street holds small dwellings, tenements, the Farmers Hotel, the Milburn Hotel, a W.C.T.U. hall, a drug store and a bakery; the Milburn Public School stands at the left edge on Milburn Avenue. East of Main Street a mill race runs beside the C. A. Lighthipe hat body mill, then marked temporarily unoccupied, past a store and post office and a barber to the creek, which winds down the right half of the sheet from a pond at the top to another pond at the bottom. The Vauxhall Inn, a hotel and blacksmith shops lie east of the creek along Milburn Avenue. An eight-inch water pipe from the Summit water works runs along Milburn Avenue and Main Street. Margins point to sheets 115 (top) and 114 (bottom and right).
notes: Elm (street) is today's Essex Street.
Milburn Avenue is printed with the alternative name Springfield Avenue; today Millburn Avenue.
D. L. & W. R. R., M. & E. Div. (today NJ Transit Morristown Line) crosses the top of the sheet; the depot and coal yard sites are rebuilt.
Drawn about 14 degrees turned against sheet 114: Millburn Avenue is drawn level across the page.
Placed from three hand-picked junctions along Main Street only (helmert).

sheet-114-1.description: The main part of sheet 114 covers the blocks south of Millburn Avenue between Spring Street and Main Street in Millburn village, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Taylor Street crosses the top of the part and Church Street the middle; Rector Street, drawn with dashed edges, runs below them from Spring Street to Main Street. Spring Street runs down the left side and Main Street along the right edge, mostly beyond the sheet. Milburn Avenue appears at the top left corner by the Baptist Church with its tower and spire. The blocks are residential with frame dwellings and a few tenements, mixed with the hat industry that gave Millburn its trade: John Ward's hat factory on Taylor Street, H. M. Graves's hat shop (temporarily closed) between Taylor and Church Streets, and F. Fouratt's hat works on Spring Street, each with sizing, coloring, pouncing and drying rooms. St. Stephen's Episcopal Church stands at Church Street and Main Street, a colored church near Taylor Street, and a florist's glass hot houses and Mechanics Hall with tenements on Spring Street. The block south of Rector Street is largely empty and marked no exposure. Margins point to sheet 113 at the top and to the two insets drawn at the bottom of the sheet.
notes: Rector (street) is drawn with dashed edges, apparently laid out but not fully opened.
Main Street lies mostly beyond the right edge; the Church Street and Rector Street junctions with it were hand-picked from its drawn west edge.
St. Stephen's Episcopal Church and the Baptist Church are drawn.

sheet-114-2.description: An inset at the lower left of sheet 114 shows the east side of Main Street opposite the end of Church Street in Millburn village, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the right; Main Street runs across the inset and Church Street meets it from above. Along Main Street stand a row of frame dwellings, a wagon shed, a dwelling with a lodge room and tin shop, and a retaining wall; behind them the creek and the mill pond, marked partly dry, fill the lower half of the inset, with a dam across it and ruins at the left edge. An eight-inch water pipe runs in Main Street. The part above Main Street is marked no exposure. The inset continues the Main Street frontage that lies beyond the right edge of the main map of the sheet.
notes: Inset turned about 90 degrees: north points to the right.

sheet-114-3.description: An inset at the lower right of sheet 114 shows a short stretch of Milburn Avenue (Springfield Avenue) east of the creek in Millburn village, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the left; Milburn Avenue runs up the inset and an unnamed street, labelled Street (No Name), meets it from the left. Both are drawn with dashed edges on the inset side. North of Milburn Avenue and east of the unnamed street stand tenements with a Chinese laundry, a building with a blacksmith shop and dwelling, and sheds; west of the unnamed street the inset is blank apart from a note giving 195 feet to the Vauxhall Inn. The block south of Milburn Avenue is blank. A 200-foot note to a frame dwelling is given at the upper left.
notes: Inset turned about 90 degrees: north points to the left.
The unnamed street is taken to be today's Lackawanna Place; the 195 ft note to the Vauxhall Inn (sheet 113) fits that if measured from the street. Low confidence.

sheet-115-1.description: The left part of sheet 115 covers Brookside Avenue and the mills north of the railroad in Millburn village, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. Brookside Avenue runs up the left side of the part from its junction with Main Street, which crosses the lower left corner diagonally to the Milburn passenger depot at the bottom edge. East of Brookside Avenue lie the Diamond Mills Paper Company's works, with machine, beating, boiling and rag and paper stock rooms, tanks, a repair shop and storage, and a mill race along the avenue. The creek winds down the middle of the part into a large mill pond that fills its lower half. A few dwellings, an ice house and sheds stand along Brookside Avenue and Main Street. A long note describes the paper company's fire protection, power and lighting. A heavy vertical line separates this part from three insets of other mills on the right half of the sheet.
notes: Brookside Avenue is today's Brookside Drive; Main north-west of the depot is today's Old Short Hills Road.
Diamond Mills Paper Co. drawn in detail.
